decision: Which approach best resolves: WF-089 must model a quote priced in a transaction currency with FX conversion into an organisation base currency. The research quotes two vendors that disagree: HubSpot price books are single-currency, so 'multi-currency is modelled as multiple price books', while Dynamics uses one transactioncurrency record plus pricelevel and pricelevelproduct rows and stores every money value twice, once in the transaction currency and once in a _Base column driven by a read-only ExchangeRate. Which product model should this codebase implement, given that the same workflow also has to refuse a wrong-currency price list with PricingErrorCode 34 and 38 and forbid changing a quote's currency while it has line items?

state.problem: WF-089 must model a quote priced in a transaction currency with FX conversion into an organisation base currency. The research quotes two vendors that disagree: HubSpot price books are single-currency, so 'multi-currency is modelled as multiple price books', while Dynamics uses one transactioncurrency record plus pricelevel and pricelevelproduct rows and stores every money value twice, once in the transaction currency and once in a _Base column driven by a read-only ExchangeRate. Which product model should this codebase implement, given that the same workflow also has to refuse a wrong-currency price list with PricingErrorCode 34 and 38 and forbid changing a quote's currency while it has line items?

candidate_solutions.dynamics_dual_currency_rows: Implement the Dynamics model. One organisation base currency record, N transaction currency records each carrying ISOCurrencyCode, CurrencySymbol, CurrencyPrecision, ExchangeRate and CurrencyType (Standard or Custom). A price list is single-currency like a HubSpot price book. A price list item is one row per product per price list, so a EUR price list and a USD price list are separate price lists rather than separate rows on one list. A quote header stamps transactioncurrencyid and the price list, and every money value is stored twice: the transaction figure and the _Base figure derived by the stamped rate. Refusals set pricingerrorcode 34 when the price list currency differs from the header currency and 38 when a line item's product has no price in the transaction currency. Changing the currency is refused with 409 while the quote holds line items.
candidate_solutions.hubspot_multiple_price_books: Implement the HubSpot model. Every currency has its own price book and a quote names one price book, so there is never a cross-currency price row. Conversion to the base currency is computed for display only at read time from the current rate rather than stored in a _Base column, and there are no pricingerrorcode values because a product simply is not in the selected book.
candidate_solutions.single_multi_currency_price_row: Implement one product price row holding a map of currency code to unit price, and let one price list serve every currency. This is the most compact shape and it removes the need for separate price lists per currency.
candidate_solutions.rates_only_no_stored_base: Implement the Dynamics header and rate model but store only the transaction currency figure, converting to the base currency on every read. This halves the stored money fields and removes the risk of a stale _Base figure.

context.spec_requires_both_money_values: The issue states: 'The spec requires both the transaction-currency figure and the _Base figure, and the read-only exchangerate and *_Base columns hold the converted base-currency view for reporting. Decide which one is authoritative for a given total and record it.'
spec_named_error_codes: 38 Transaction currency is not set for the product price list item
sourced_evidence: Your base record and all its line items must use the same currency. You can't change the currency of the base record (in this case, an quote), unless you remove all the line items associated with the record.
ExchangeRate - Shows the conversion rate of the record's currency. The exchange rate is used to convert all money fields in the record from the local currency to the system's default currency.
PricingErrorCode option 38: Transaction currency is not set for the product price list item; option 34: Invalid Price Level Currency.
Click the Currencies dropdown menu and select a currency (HubSpot price books are single-currency).
repository_constraints: The feature adds files and edits no shared file.
Records are arbitrary JSON in records.data with no migration and no typed column.
Every write goes through AuditedDatabase, so the audit row is in the same transaction.

The quote record itself is provisioned by WF-086 and the price list by WF-087, neither of which is implemented yet, so this workflow must be able to read quote and price rows written by another workflow as data.
context.prior_features_in_this_repository: WF-085 shipped dual figure storage for its own records and records each judgement call with the alternative it rejected, served over HTTP at /decisions.

decision: Implementation of WF-089 meets the release bar

state.change_summary: WF-089 ships as a feature plugin that adds files only. backend/dsr/quote_currency/ holds the domain module: vocabulary.py carries every constant named after the researched specification, errors.py declares the four error types this workflow raises, rules.py holds the decimal money arithmetic, the one rate direction and the two pricing refusals, inferences.py records ten judgement calls with the alternative each rejected, and engine.py is the workflow over RecordStore. backend/dsr/features/wf089_quote_in_a_transaction_currency_with_fx.py exports FEATURE, a router on prefix /api/wf-089 with 19 routes, four exception handlers and seed(db, context). frontend/src/features/wf-089-quote-in-a-transaction-currency-with-fx-conversion/ holds index.jsx, api.js, primitives.jsx and a 39-test suite. The workflow prices a quote in a transaction currency, computes every total in that currency and derives every *_Base figure from it by the rate stamped on the quote, and refuses a wrong-currency price list with PricingErrorCode 34 and a line item with no price in the transaction currency with PricingErrorCode 38. Both refusals answer 200 with outcome refused, write an audit row exactly as a successful run does, and clear every money figure so no partial total can be mistaken for a priced quote. The domain package imports dsr.store and nothing else inside dsr; the feature module imports dsr.deps and never dsr.api; no shared file is edited.
